sides.text: Four laws that unify electricity and magnetism

more.text: Gauss (electric): ∇·E = ρ/ε₀. Gauss (magnetic): ∇·B = 0. Faraday: ∇×E = −∂B/∂t. Ampère–Maxwell: ∇×B = μ₀J + μ₀ε₀ ∂E/∂t.

sides.text: Which Maxwell equation says a changing magnetic field creates an electric field?

more.text: Faraday's law.
Maxwell found that electromagnetic waves travel at a speed set by the permeability and permittivity of free space, matching the measured speed of light.

sides.text: What two constants set the speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum?

more.text: Permeability (μ₀) and permittivity (ε₀) of free space.
The ratio of electric to magnetic field in a plane wave in vacuum. It sets reflection at material boundaries.

sides.text: What is the impedance of free space?

more.text: About 377 Ω.

sides.text: S = E × H: power flow of a wave

more.text: Gives the direction and density (W/m²) of electromagnetic power flow. Averaging over time gives the intensity.

sides.text: What does the Poynting vector represent?

more.text: Power flow per unit area of an electromagnetic wave.
How deep current penetrates a conductor. Higher frequency or conductivity gives a smaller depth.

sides.text: What happens to skin depth as frequency rises?

more.text: It decreases.
For normal incidence, Γ = (η₂ − η₁)/(η₂ + η₁). A wave entering a conductor is mostly reflected.

sides.text: What causes a wave to reflect at a boundary between two materials?

more.text: A difference in wave impedance.

sides.text: A hollow metal tube that guides microwaves

more.text: Below the cutoff frequency waves don't propagate. For the TE₁₀ mode in an air-filled guide, f_c = c / (2a), where a is the wide dimension.

sides.text: a = 2.286 cm waveguide. What is the TE₁₀ cutoff?

more.text: In the far field the fields fall as 1/r and the power density as 1/r². A half-wave dipole has a radiation resistance of about 73 Ω.

sides.text: What is a half-wave dipole's approximate radiation resistance?

more.text: About 73 Ω.
The area an antenna effectively captures. Higher gain or longer wavelength means more captured power.

sides.text: Which antenna parameter relates gain to effective capture area?

more.text: Effective aperture.

sides.text: Combine elements to shape and steer a beam

more.text: The array factor depends on element spacing and phase. Phase shifts steer the beam electronically (phased arrays).

sides.text: How does a phased array steer its beam?

more.text: By adjusting the phase of each element.

sides.text: Range from echo delay; speed from Doppler

more.text: Range resolution is c / (2B), where B is the signal bandwidth. Doppler shift reveals radial velocity.

sides.text: A radar uses 150 MHz of bandwidth. What is its range resolution?

more.text: About 1 m.
The first stage dominates, so a low-noise, high-gain amplifier belongs at the receiver front end.

sides.text: Why does the first stage dominate a receiver's noise figure?

more.text: Later stages' noise is divided by the gain ahead of them.
Unconditional stability needs K > 1 and |Δ| < 1 (from S-parameters). Resistive loading or feedback can restore it.

sides.text: What can an RF amplifier do if it's potentially unstable?

more.text: Oscillate, unless stabilized with resistive loading or feedback.
Appears as skirts around the carrier in the spectrum (dBc/Hz). It limits receiver selectivity and modulation quality. Leeson's model relates it to Q and noise.

sides.text: Where does oscillator phase noise appear in the spectrum?

more.text: As skirts around the carrier.

sides.text: Loop bandwidth sets lock time and noise

more.text: An integer-N PLL has f_out = N × f_ref. Fractional-N gives finer steps using a sigma-delta divider. A phase margin near 45–60° gives stable lock.

sides.text: How does an integer-N PLL set its output frequency?

more.text: f_out = N × f_ref.

sides.text:
Conversion gain
LO leakage
image rejection

more.text: Image frequencies fall on the other side of the LO and must be filtered or cancelled (image-reject mixers).

sides.text: What is the image frequency problem?

more.text: A second frequency also mixes to the same IF and must be rejected.
High-efficiency classes (E, F) switch the device but distort. Digital pre-distortion linearizes amplifiers for complex modulation.

sides.text: What technique linearizes an RF power amplifier digitally?

more.text: Digital pre-distortion (DPD).

sides.text: Distance between ideal and received constellation points

more.text: Summarizes the quality of a modulated signal, combining noise, distortion, and phase noise. Standards set EVM limits.
How far received constellation points are from their ideal positions.
Valid in saturation for long-channel devices. Wider or shorter devices carry more current.

sides.text: μCox = 100 µA/V², W/L = 20, and Vov = 0.2 V. What is I_D?

more.text: Drain current rises slightly with Vds, limiting the intrinsic gain g_m × r_o. Longer channels give higher r_o.

sides.text: Which transistor dimension increases output resistance when lengthened?

more.text: Channel length.
The maximum gain from a single transistor. Falls in advanced processes, so designers use cascodes and gain boosting.

sides.text: What limits the gain of a single-transistor stage?

more.text: The transistor's intrinsic gain g_m × r_o.

sides.text: High gain with good output swing

more.text: Folds the cascode current path so the input and output sit at different DC levels, allowing a wide input range at low supply voltage.

sides.text: What advantage does the folded cascode have over the telescopic cascode?

more.text: Better input common-mode range and output swing at low supply voltage.

sides.text: Pole splitting in a two-stage op-amp

more.text: A capacitor across the second stage moves the dominant pole lower and the second pole higher, for stability. A right-half-plane zero may need a nulling resistor.

sides.text: What does Miller compensation do to the poles?

more.text: Splits them apart: dominant pole lower, second pole higher.

sides.text: A voltage nearly independent of temperature

more.text: Adds a PTAT voltage (rises with T) to a CTAT voltage (falls with T). The result is about 1.2 V.

sides.text: What two temperature behaviors does a bandgap reference combine?

more.text: PTAT and CTAT.

sides.text: Pass transistor in a feedback loop

more.text: The output capacitor and its ESR affect loop stability. PSRR and dropout are key specs.

sides.text: What affects an LDO's loop stability besides the amplifier?

more.text: The output capacitor and its ESR.

sides.text: A switched capacitor acts like a resistor

more.text: R_eq = 1 / (f_s × C). Precise ratios of capacitors give accurate gain and filters on-chip.

sides.text: C = 1 pF and f_s = 1 MHz. What is the equivalent resistance?

more.text: 1 MΩ.
In a first-order modulator, each doubling of the oversampling ratio gains about 9 dB (about 1.5 bits). Second order gains about 15 dB.

sides.text: About how much SQNR does doubling OSR give a first-order delta-sigma modulator?

more.text: About 9 dB.
Pelgrom's law: mismatch ∝ 1/√(W·L). Common-centroid layout cancels gradients.

sides.text: What layout technique cancels linear process gradients?

more.text: Common-centroid layout.
Verify performance at slow, typical, and fast process corners, across supply and temperature ranges, plus Monte Carlo for mismatch.
Process, voltage, and temperature.

sides.text: Refer noise to the input to compare amplifiers

more.text: Thermal noise voltage of a transistor is about 4kTγ/g_m per hertz. Larger g_m (more current) lowers it.

sides.text: What reduces a transistor's thermal input noise?

more.text: Higher transconductance g_m.
ENOB = (SINAD − 1.76) / 6.02. DNL measures step-size errors; INL the total deviation from an ideal line.

sides.text: SINAD = 62 dB. What is the ENOB?

more.text: About 10 bits.
Sampling-time jitter limits the SNR for high-frequency inputs.

sides.text: f_in = 10 MHz and σ_t = 1 ps. What SNR limit does the jitter set?

more.text: About 84 dB.
Silicon's bandgap is 1.12 eV, GaAs 1.42 eV, SiC about 3.3 eV, and GaN about 3.4 eV. A wider gap means higher breakdown voltage and temperature tolerance.

sides.text: Why do SiC and GaN suit high-voltage, high-temperature devices?

more.text: Their wide bandgaps give high breakdown fields and low leakage.
The product of electron and hole concentrations is constant at a given temperature. Doping one raises its concentration and lowers the other.

sides.text: What happens to hole concentration when you dope heavily n-type?

more.text: It falls, since n × p stays at nᵢ².
The potential barrier across a PN junction at equilibrium. About 0.6 to 0.8 V in silicon.

sides.text: What sets the barrier voltage of a PN junction?

more.text: The doping levels, through V_bi.
Current rises exponentially with forward voltage. I_s depends strongly on temperature, so the forward drop falls about 2 mV/°C.

sides.text: I_s = 1 pA, V = 0.6 V, n = 1, V_T = 25.85 mV. About what current?

more.text: About 12 mA.

sides.text: Complementary pair: almost no static power

more.text: When the input is static one transistor is off. Power is used mainly while switching: P = α C V² f.

sides.text: α = 0.1, C = 1 nF, V = 1 V, f = 1 GHz. What is the dynamic power?

more.text: Gate delay depends on drive strength and the load it sees. Sizing gates for the load (logical effort) minimizes path delay.

sides.text: What does gate delay mostly depend on?

more.text: The drive resistance times the load capacitance.
Subthreshold, gate-oxide tunneling, and junction leakage rise as transistors shrink and thresholds fall. Techniques: power gating and multiple thresholds.

sides.text: Which technique cuts leakage by disconnecting idle blocks?

more.text: Power gating.

sides.text: Scaling gave faster, cooler chips, until it didn't

more.text: Dennard scaling (1974) held power density constant as transistors shrank. It broke down in the mid-2000s from leakage, ending easy clock gains. Moore's law (transistor counts) continued longer.

sides.text: Why did clock speeds stop rising steadily in the mid-2000s?

more.text: Dennard scaling broke down as leakage grew.

sides.text: Better gate control at small sizes

more.text: A FinFET wraps the gate around a fin on three sides. Gate-all-around (nanosheet) surrounds the channel fully for even better control and less leakage.

sides.text: Which transistor structure surrounds the channel on all sides?

more.text: Gate-all-around.
193 nm immersion DUV is the workhorse for many layers. EUV at 13.5 nm prints the finest features. Multi-patterning extends DUV.

sides.text: What wavelength does EUV lithography use?
Deposit, pattern, etch, dope, polish, repeat

more.text: Photolithography defines features. Etching removes material. Deposition adds films. Ion implantation sets doping. CMP flattens surfaces.

sides.text: Which step planarizes the wafer between layers?

more.text: Chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP).
The Poisson model: yield falls exponentially with die area and defect density. Smaller dies yield better.

sides.text: Why do smaller dies have better yield?

more.text: A smaller area means fewer defects per die.
Chiplets are combined on an interposer or stacked to increase bandwidth and mix process nodes. High-bandwidth memory (HBM) is stacked next to the processor.
Smaller dies combined in one package to act as a system.
SRAM: 6 transistors, fast, no refresh. DRAM: 1 transistor and 1 capacitor, needs refresh. NAND flash: charge trapped on a floating gate or charge-trap layer.

sides.text: How many transistors does a standard SRAM cell use?

more.text: Six.

sides.text: Voltage mode vs peak current mode

more.text: Voltage mode uses one loop. Peak current mode adds a fast inner current loop, simplifying compensation and giving cycle-by-cycle current limiting. Current mode needs slope compensation above 50% duty.

sides.text: Which control mode gives inherent cycle-by-cycle current limiting?

more.text: Peak current mode.
In CCM boost and buck-boost converters, a right-half-plane zero adds phase lag while raising gain, limiting achievable loop bandwidth to a fraction of the zero frequency.

sides.text: Which converter topologies have a right-half-plane zero in CCM?

more.text: Boost and buck-boost (and flyback).

sides.text: Model a switching converter as a continuous system

more.text: Average the on and off state equations by duty cycle, then linearize around an operating point to get transfer functions for compensation design.

sides.text: Why average a converter's switching states?

more.text: To obtain a continuous small-signal model for loop design.
An LLC converter switches near resonance so transistors turn on at zero voltage (ZVS), cutting switching loss and EMI. Common in power supplies for TVs and servers.
Switching loss at turn-on.

sides.text: Core loss and saturation limit size

more.text: Steinmetz's equation estimates core loss. An air gap raises saturation current. Turns follow N = √(L / A_L).

sides.text: What is the purpose of an air gap in a power inductor core?

more.text: To raise the current at which the core saturates.
Thermal RC networks describe how junction temperature rises over time. Short pulses see lower temperature rise than steady power.

sides.text: Why can a MOSFET survive a short overload that would destroy it continuously?

more.text: Thermal capacitance limits the temperature rise in short pulses (low Z_th).
Transform three-phase quantities into a rotating frame where AC variables become DC, so torque and flux can be controlled with simple PI loops (field-oriented control).

sides.text: What does the Park transform give field-oriented control?

more.text: A rotating frame where AC quantities appear as DC.

sides.text: Better DC-bus use for three-phase inverters

more.text: Treats the three phases as one rotating vector and synthesizes it from adjacent switching states, giving about 15% more output voltage than sinusoidal PWM.

sides.text: What advantage does SVPWM have over sinusoidal PWM?

more.text: About 15% higher usable voltage from the same DC bus.

sides.text: Set the voltage vs follow it

more.text: Grid-following inverters synchronize to an existing grid. Grid-forming inverters create their own voltage and frequency, providing stability in weak or islanded grids.

sides.text: Which inverter type can start up and hold an islanded microgrid?

more.text: Grid-forming.
The rotor accelerates in proportion to the imbalance between mechanical and electrical power. It underlies transient and frequency stability.

sides.text: What does the swing equation describe?

more.text: How a generator's rotor angle changes when power is unbalanced.
Line-commutated (thyristor) converters handle huge power but need a strong grid. Voltage-source (IGBT) converters can black-start and control reactive power independently.

sides.text: Which HVDC converter type can black-start a grid?

more.text: Voltage-source converters (VSC).
A voltage source (OCV vs SoC), a series resistance, and RC networks capture dynamics. Thermal runaway occurs when heat triggers self-reinforcing reactions.

sides.text: What event is a self-reinforcing heat rise in a Li-ion cell?

more.text: Thermal runaway.
Charging at high rates and low temperature can plate lithium on the anode, reducing capacity and creating safety risk. Chargers taper current and manage temperature.

sides.text: What risk does fast charging at low temperature add?

more.text: Lithium plating.
UN 38.3 covers transport testing. IEC 62619 covers industrial lithium cells. UL 1973 covers stationary batteries and UL 9540 covers energy storage systems.

sides.text: Which test standard covers transporting lithium batteries?

more.text: Clearance is the shortest path through air; creepage is along a surface. Both grow with voltage and pollution degree. Reinforced isolation uses larger spacing.

sides.text: Which distance follows the surface of an insulator?

more.text: Creepage.

sides.text: Where a device can safely operate

more.text: Limits from current, voltage, power, and thermal behavior (including linear-mode second breakdown). Avalanche energy ratings handle brief overvoltage.

sides.text: What does a SOA curve define?

more.text: The voltage and current combinations a device can handle safely.
High dV/dt can turn the opposite switch on via the Miller capacitance. Use negative off-state gate voltage and low-inductance layouts.

sides.text: What can high dV/dt do in a half-bridge?

more.text: Couple through the Miller capacitance and falsely turn on the other switch.
Data, control, and structural hazards stall or flush a pipeline. Forwarding and branch prediction mitigate them.

sides.text: What kind of hazard does a mispredicted branch cause?

more.text: A control hazard, flushing the pipeline.

sides.text: Keep CPU and peripherals' views consistent

more.text: DMA writes memory behind the CPU's cache, so software must invalidate or clean cache lines or use non-cacheable regions.

sides.text: Why might the CPU read stale data after a DMA transfer on a cached system?

more.text: The cache still holds old data. Invalidate it first.
Compilers and CPUs reorder accesses. Barriers (DMB, DSB, ISB on Arm) make sure writes complete before a dependent action.
The order and completion of memory accesses.
Separate head and tail indexes updated by one side each need no lock, provided accesses are atomic and ordered.

sides.text: What makes a single-producer single-consumer ring buffer lock-free?

more.text: Each index is written by only one side.

sides.text: TrustZone-M and hardware root of trust

more.text: Hardware splits memory and peripherals into secure and non-secure worlds. A hardware root of trust (immutable ROM and keys) anchors secure boot.

sides.text: What anchors a secure boot chain?

more.text: A hardware root of trust.

sides.text: Leaking secrets through power or timing

more.text: Power analysis and timing differences can reveal cryptographic keys. Countermeasures: constant-time code, masking, and noise.
Physical leakage like power use or timing.
Voltage or clock glitches can skip instructions such as a security check. Mitigations: brown-out detectors, redundancy, and checksums.

sides.text: What does a voltage glitch attack try to do?

more.text: Make the chip skip or corrupt an instruction.

sides.text: Run the task with the nearest deadline

more.text: EDF is optimal for single-processor preemptive scheduling and can reach 100% utilization, but fails less gracefully under overload.

sides.text: Which scheduler can achieve 100% utilization on one core?

more.text: Earliest deadline first (EDF).
Computes each task's response time including preemption by higher-priority tasks, to check deadlines.
That tasks meet their deadlines in the worst case.

sides.text: Cross clock domains with Gray-coded pointers

more.text: Gray code changes one bit at a time, so synchronizing pointers can't be caught in a wrong intermediate value.

sides.text: Why use Gray code for FIFO pointers across clock domains?

more.text: Only one bit changes at a time, avoiding invalid values.
Float32 uses 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits, and 23 fraction bits. Double uses 1, 11, and 52.

sides.text: How many exponent bits does a float32 have?
Qm.n integers with an implied binary point

more.text: Q15 has 1 sign bit and 15 fractional bits, covering −1 to 1 − 2⁻¹⁵. Multiplying needs a shift to rescale.
−1 to just under +1.
Models are quantized (often to int8) and run with small runtimes such as TensorFlow Lite Micro. Used for keyword spotting and anomaly detection.

sides.text: Which numeric format commonly shrinks models for microcontrollers?

more.text: 8-bit integers (int8 quantization).
IEC 61508: general functional safety. ISO 26262: automotive, with ASIL A to D. DO-178C: airborne software. MISRA C: coding rules for safety.

sides.text: Which standard covers automotive functional safety?

more.text: Each block survives a limited number of erase cycles. Wear leveling spreads writes across blocks.
Spreads writes to extend flash life.
NTP gives millisecond accuracy over the internet. IEEE 1588 PTP with hardware timestamps reaches sub-microsecond accuracy.

sides.text: Which protocol reaches sub-microsecond time synchronization?

more.text: PTP (IEEE 1588).
The average information per symbol, in bits. A fair coin has 1 bit. Predictable sources have lower entropy.

sides.text: What is the entropy of a coin that lands heads 25% of the time?

more.text: About 0.81 bits.
Channel capacity is the maximum mutual information over input distributions. For the Gaussian channel it's B log₂(1 + SNR).
Mutual information between input and output.

sides.text: Compress to entropy; send reliably below capacity

more.text: Source coding: you can't compress below the entropy. Channel coding: reliable communication is possible at any rate below capacity.

sides.text: Is error-free communication possible above channel capacity?

more.text: No.
The minimum distance between codewords sets how many errors can be detected (d_min − 1) and corrected.

sides.text: A code has d_min = 7. How many errors can it correct?

more.text: Work on multi-bit symbols, so they correct bursts. Used in CDs, QR codes, and deep-space links.

sides.text: Which code family is used in QR codes and CDs?

more.text: Reed–Solomon.
Iterative decoding gets within a fraction of a dB of capacity. LDPC is used in Wi-Fi and 5G data channels.

sides.text: Which code decodes iteratively and nears the Shannon limit?

more.text: LDPC (and turbo) codes.
Capacity grows with the number of independent spatial paths (rank of the channel matrix H).

sides.text: What determines how much MIMO capacity grows?

more.text: The rank of the channel matrix, set by independent spatial paths.
Combining N elements coherently adds N times the power in the target direction.
About 12 dB.
Subcarrier spacing is the inverse of the useful symbol time. IFFT builds the signal. 5G scales spacing in powers of two from 15 kHz.
The inverse of the useful symbol duration.
Known pilot symbols let the receiver estimate fading and equalize data subcarriers.

sides.text: What do pilot symbols allow a receiver to do?

more.text: Estimate the channel so it can equalize the data.
The Costas loop recovers carrier phase for PSK. The Gardner detector recovers symbol timing without knowing the data.

sides.text: Which loop recovers carrier phase for BPSK without a pilot?

more.text: The Costas loop.
Minimizes mean squared error between the desired signal and the filter output, using signal and noise statistics.

sides.text: What does a Wiener filter minimize?

more.text: The mean squared error.

sides.text: Predict, then update with the measurement

more.text: For a scalar case, K = P / (P + R). The gain weighs prediction uncertainty against measurement noise. Optimal for linear systems with Gaussian noise.

sides.text: Predicted variance P = 4 and measurement noise R = 4. What is the Kalman gain?

more.text: Recursive least squares converges faster than LMS but costs more computation per sample.

sides.text: Which adaptive filter converges faster but costs more?

more.text: RLS.
The periodogram has high variance. Welch's method averages windowed segments to cut variance at some cost in resolution.

sides.text: Which method averages segments to reduce periodogram variance?

more.text: Welch's method.
The receiver measures pseudoranges to at least four satellites to solve for 3D position and its own clock error.

sides.text: Why does GPS need four satellites?

more.text: Three coordinates plus the receiver clock bias.

sides.text: Long delays and large path loss

more.text: A GEO satellite is about 36,000 km up. The ground–satellite–ground path adds about 240 ms one way. LEO constellations cut latency.

sides.text: About how much one-way delay does a GEO link add?

more.text: About 240 ms.
Coherent receivers recover amplitude and phase on two polarizations with DSP, using formats like DP-QPSK and DP-16QAM at hundreds of Gbit/s per wavelength.

sides.text: What do coherent optical receivers recover?

more.text: Amplitude and phase on both polarizations.
Minimizes a quadratic cost on state and control effort by solving a Riccati equation. Gives gain K for u = −Kx.
A quadratic cost of state error and control effort.
A Luenberger observer corrects a model's state estimate using the measurement error. The Kalman filter is the optimal stochastic version.
The system's unmeasured states.
Solves a constrained optimization at each step and applies the first move. Used for converters, motors, and process control.

sides.text: What distinguishes MPC from fixed-gain controllers?

more.text: It re-optimizes over a future horizon with constraints each step.
For minimum-phase systems, a −20 dB/decade slope near crossover corresponds to about −90° phase, giving good margin. A steeper slope risks instability.

sides.text: What slope should the loop gain have near crossover for good phase margin?

more.text: About −20 dB/decade.

sides.text: Convert a continuous controller to digital

more.text: The bilinear (Tustin) transform maps s to z while preserving stability and warping frequency. Sample fast compared with the bandwidth.

sides.text: Which transform keeps a stable analog design stable in the z-domain?

more.text: The bilinear (Tustin) transform.
Saturation and backlash can cause sustained oscillation (limit cycles). Anti-windup freezes or back-calculates the integrator when the actuator saturates.
The integrator growing while the actuator is saturated.
Flyback suits low power, forward and push-pull mid power, and full-bridge the highest. Half-bridge halves the voltage across the transformer. Push-pull needs care to avoid flux imbalance.

sides.text: Which isolated topology is typical for kilowatt-class supplies?

more.text: The full-bridge.

sides.text: Zero-voltage switching by shifting the legs

more.text: Uses transformer leakage inductance and switch capacitances so each switch turns on at zero voltage. Common in server and telecom power.

sides.text: What does the phase shift control in a phase-shifted full bridge?

more.text: The power transferred, while enabling soft switching.
Two H-bridges linked by a transformer and inductor. The phase shift between them sets the direction and amount of power. Used in battery storage and EV chargers.

sides.text: Which topology gives bidirectional isolated power flow set by phase shift?

more.text: The dual active bridge.
N phases offset by 360°/N cancel ripple, and spread the heat. Input and output filters shrink.

sides.text: A 4-phase interleaved buck converter. What is the phase offset?

more.text: NPC, flying capacitor, and cascaded H-bridge inverters produce stepped waveforms with lower dv/dt and distortion, useful at medium and high voltage.

sides.text: What advantage do multilevel inverters give at high voltage?

more.text: Lower harmonic distortion and dv/dt with smaller filters.
Many identical submodules, each a bridge with a capacitor, build a nearly sinusoidal voltage. Dominant in modern voltage-source HVDC.

sides.text: Which converter type dominates modern VSC-HVDC?

more.text: The modular multilevel converter (MMC).
Rectifiers and other nonlinear loads draw harmonic currents. IEEE 519 sets limits at the point of common coupling.

sides.text: V₁ = 100 V with a 5 V fifth harmonic and 3 V seventh. What is the THD?

more.text: About 5.8%.

sides.text: Unbalanced faults as three balanced sets

more.text: Fortescue's method splits an unbalanced system into positive, negative, and zero sequence components. Fault types connect the sequence networks differently.

sides.text: Into which three sequences are unbalanced systems decomposed?

more.text: Positive, negative, and zero sequence.
Given P and Q at load buses and P and |V| at generator buses, Newton–Raphson iterates for the voltages and angles.

sides.text: Which method is standard for power flow studies?

more.text: Newton–Raphson.

sides.text: A relay measures impedance to a fault

more.text: Zone 1 usually covers about 80 to 85% of a line instantly. Later zones add time-delayed backup.

sides.text: What does a distance relay measure?

more.text: The impedance between the relay and the fault.
Inrush looks like an internal fault, so relays use second-harmonic restraint to avoid false trips.

sides.text: Why do transformer relays use second-harmonic restraint?

more.text: To distinguish magnetizing inrush from a real internal fault.

sides.text: Generators regulate voltage with field current

more.text: An automatic voltage regulator adjusts field current. Power system stabilizers add damping to oscillations.
The generator's field (excitation) current.
P–f and Q–V droop let generators and inverters in parallel split load. A 5% droop machine falls 5% in frequency from no load to full load.

sides.text: A 5% droop generator at 60 Hz no load. What is its frequency at full load?

more.text: 57 Hz.
Grids with many inverter-based sources have less inertia, so frequency changes faster after a disturbance (higher rate of change of frequency).

sides.text: What happens to RoCoF when grid inertia falls?

more.text: It rises.
Combine generation, storage, and loads. They operate connected or islanded and need grid-forming control to hold voltage and frequency.

sides.text: What must a microgrid have to operate islanded?

more.text: Grid-forming control.
An extended Kalman filter fuses a cell model with voltage and current measurements to estimate state of charge and health.

sides.text: Which estimator is commonly used for battery SoC?

more.text: An extended Kalman filter.

sides.text: Burn excess charge or move it

more.text: Passive balancing bleeds high cells through resistors. Active balancing transfers charge with converters, saving energy.

sides.text: Which balancing method wastes energy as heat?

more.text: Passive balancing.

sides.text: Coupling coefficient and Q set efficiency

more.text: Resonant compensation networks tune the coils. Qi runs at roughly 100 to 205 kHz. Efficiency falls quickly as coupling k drops.

sides.text: What two parameters mainly set wireless power efficiency?

more.text: Coupling coefficient and quality factor.

sides.text: Estimate rotor position without a sensor

more.text: Back-EMF observers work above a minimum speed. At low speed, signal injection is used.

sides.text: Why can't back-EMF methods work at standstill?

more.text: Back-EMF is proportional to speed and is zero at standstill.
IEC 60034-30 defines classes. IE3 is premium efficiency and IE4 is super-premium.

sides.text: Which efficiency class is higher, IE3 or IE4?

more.text: IE4.
Stray capacitances conduct high-frequency current through motor bearings and cables. Output filters, shielded cables, and grounding rings reduce it.

sides.text: What causes bearing damage in inverter-fed motors?

more.text: High-frequency common-mode currents through the bearings.
Fast switching with stray inductance causes voltage spikes. Keep the loop area small.

sides.text: A 10 nH loop switches at 1 A/ns. How large is the spike?
Reduce AC resistance in high-frequency windings

more.text: Litz wire uses many insulated strands. Proximity effect from neighboring layers raises loss even when skin depth is large.
AC resistance from skin and proximity effects.
Film capacitors have low ESR and long life. Electrolytics are dense but wear out and heat under ripple.

sides.text: Which DC-link capacitor type lasts longer under ripple current?

more.text: Film.
The Arrhenius rule of thumb for electrolytic capacitors. The bathtub curve shows early, random, and wear-out failures.

sides.text: By how much does a 10 °C rise typically shorten electrolytic capacitor life?

more.text: About by half.
Turning on at zero voltage or off at zero current removes switching loss and EMI, at the cost of circulating current and complexity.
Turn-on switching loss.
High-side switches need a floating gate drive. Isolated drivers handle high voltages and noise immunity.

sides.text: What does a bootstrap circuit do for a high-side gate driver?

more.text: Provides a floating supply for the high-side gate.
Total input noise combines the op-amp's voltage noise, its current noise times the source resistance, and resistor thermal noise. Choose a device matched to the source impedance.

sides.text: What dominates a low-impedance source's noise: voltage or current noise of the op-amp?

more.text: The op-amp's voltage noise.
They modulate the signal above the 1/f region, amplify, then demodulate, giving offsets of microvolts or less.

sides.text: What error do chopper amplifiers minimize?

more.text: Input offset and its drift.
A matched thin-film network tracks within a few ppm/°C, keeping ratios stable even when absolute values drift.

sides.text: Why use matched resistor networks in precision amplifiers?

more.text: Their ratio stays accurate over temperature.
The feedback resistor sets gain. A small feedback capacitor stabilizes it against the photodiode's capacitance.

sides.text: What stabilizes a TIA against input capacitance?

more.text: A small capacitor across the feedback resistor.
Sampling a capacitor leaves thermal noise that depends only on C and temperature. Larger capacitors give less noise.

sides.text: C = 1 pF at 300 K. What is the rms noise?

more.text: About 64 µV.
Droop, charge injection, and aperture jitter limit accuracy. A larger hold capacitor reduces droop but slows tracking.

sides.text: What does aperture jitter affect in a sample-and-hold?

more.text: The timing accuracy of the sample.

sides.text: Output proportional to the log of the input

more.text: Uses a diode or BJT in the feedback path. Compresses a wide dynamic range, such as in RF power detectors.

sides.text: What advantage does a log amplifier offer?

more.text: It compresses a very wide input range into a small output range.

sides.text: An op-amp cancels the diode drop

more.text: Lets circuits rectify signals smaller than 0.7 V. Used in AC measurement.
To rectify small signals without the diode's forward drop.

sides.text: Output current set by input voltage

more.text: gm is tunable by a bias current, so OTAs build tunable filters and oscillators (gm-C designs).

sides.text: What does an OTA's output current depend on?

more.text: The input voltage times its transconductance.

sides.text: Motional RLC with a shunt capacitance

more.text: Has series and parallel resonance. The load capacitance specified by the manufacturer pulls the oscillation frequency.

sides.text: What sets a crystal's exact oscillation frequency in a circuit?

more.text: The load capacitance it sees (together with its cut).

sides.text: Frequency set by a control voltage

more.text: Varactor-tuned LC VCOs have low phase noise. Ring VCOs are compact but noisier.

sides.text: Which VCO type usually has lower phase noise: LC or ring?

more.text: LC.
Frequency resolution is f_clk / 2ᴺ for an N-bit accumulator. Fast switching and fine steps, with spurs.

sides.text: A 100 MHz clock and a 32-bit accumulator. What is the frequency resolution?

more.text: About 0.023 Hz.
Separate force and sense leads remove lead and contact resistance, essential for milliohm measurements.

sides.text: Why use four-wire sensing for a milliohm resistor?

more.text: It removes the error from lead and contact resistance.
Guard rings at the same potential intercept leakage. Clean boards and low-leakage materials help.

sides.text: What does a guard ring do around a high-impedance node?

more.text: Intercepts leakage by sitting at the same potential.
The power distribution network must stay below the target impedance across frequency, using bulk, ceramic, and on-die capacitance.

sides.text: A 1 V rail with ±5% tolerance and a 5 A step. What is the target impedance?

more.text: 10 mΩ.
Termination absorbs reflections on fast lines. Series termination is simple. Parallel gives clean edges but burns power.
Parallel termination.
Keep pairs tightly coupled, equal length, and over a continuous reference plane.

sides.text: What must a differential pair keep equal for good signal integrity?

more.text: Length (and spacing).
Eye height and width reveal noise and jitter margins. A closed eye means errors.

sides.text: What does a wide, tall eye indicate?

more.text: Good signal quality with margin.

sides.text: Serialize and deserialize with an embedded clock

more.text: Line codes like 8b/10b or 64b/66b ensure transitions so a clock-recovery circuit can lock.

sides.text: Why does SerDes use line coding?

more.text: To guarantee transitions for clock recovery.
Human-body and charged-device models cover chip handling. IEC 61000-4-2 covers system-level discharges at connectors.

sides.text: Which model describes a charged chip discharging to ground?

more.text: The charged-device model (CDM).

sides.text: A parasitic thyristor shorts the supply

more.text: Triggered by current injected into a pin or substrate. Guard rings and layout rules prevent it.
A parasitic thyristor (PNPN) in the chip.
Scan chains let testers shift in and read out states. Built-in self-test checks memories and logic on chip.

sides.text: What lets testers control and observe internal flip-flops?

more.text: Scan chains.
Computes delays across all paths and checks setup and hold at each flip-flop across corners.

sides.text: What does static timing analysis check?

more.text: Setup and hold timing on all paths.
Dynamic power ∝ C V² f, so reducing V and f together saves far more than reducing f alone.

sides.text: Why does DVFS save more than lowering frequency alone?

more.text: Power falls with the square of voltage.

sides.text: Keep return currents out of sensitive circuits

more.text: Place analog and digital sections apart, and use one solid ground plane with controlled return paths rather than split planes.

sides.text: What matters most when partitioning mixed-signal layouts?

more.text: Controlling where return currents flow.
Capacitive or magnetic coupling gives 2.5 to 5 kV isolation, faster and longer-lived than optocouplers.

sides.text: Which isolation technology is faster than an optocoupler?

more.text: Capacitive or magnetic digital isolators.

sides.text: The longest a task can take

more.text: Needed to prove deadlines. Caches, branch prediction, and interrupts make it hard to bound, so safety systems use simpler cores.

sides.text: Why do safety-critical systems often avoid caches?

more.text: They make worst-case timing hard to bound.
Each resource has a ceiling equal to its highest-priority user. A task locking it runs at that ceiling.

sides.text: What does the priority ceiling protocol prevent?

more.text: Priority inversion and deadlock.

sides.text: Hardware key storage and true randomness

more.text: A secure element stores keys and runs crypto in tamper-resistant hardware. A true random number generator uses physical noise.

sides.text: What does a TRNG use to create randomness?

more.text: A physical noise source.
Offload encryption from the CPU, saving time and energy and reducing side-channel exposure.

sides.text: Why use a hardware AES engine?

more.text: It's faster and uses less energy than software.
NAND flash has bit errors and bad blocks, so controllers use ECC and bad-block management. NOR is more reliable per bit.

sides.text: Which flash type usually requires ECC, NAND or NOR?

more.text: NAND.
littlefs provides wear leveling and power-loss safety on small flash. FAT is simple but can corrupt on power loss.

sides.text: Which filesystem is designed for power-loss safety on small flash?

more.text: littlefs.
Use write-ahead logs, atomic renames, or double-buffered records with checksums so a power cut leaves a valid copy.

sides.text: How can a device keep config valid across a power cut?

more.text: Write a new copy with a checksum, then switch atomically.
Separating hardware access from logic lets you test the application on a PC and port to new chips.

sides.text: Why separate hardware access into a HAL?

more.text: So application code is portable and testable.
The firmware runs on target hardware connected to a simulator that mimics sensors and actuators, enabling safe repeatable tests.
Real controller hardware with a simulated plant.

sides.text: Unit tests and CI for firmware
Test logic on a host and build automatically

more.text: Mock hardware, run tests on every commit, and cross-compile for the target in CI.

sides.text: Why run firmware logic tests on a PC?

more.text: They're faster and run on every change.

sides.text: Find defects and enforce safe C

more.text: Tools check rules such as no recursion and no dynamic allocation in safety code.
Rules for safe, portable C code in embedded systems.
Code lives in flash, initialized variables are copied to RAM at startup, and the vector table sits at a known address.

sides.text: Which section holds initialized global variables?

more.text: The .data section.
The reset handler sets the stack pointer, copies .data to RAM, zeroes .bss, configures clocks, and then calls main().

sides.text: What does startup code do with .bss?

more.text: Zeroes it.
A bootloader sets the vector table offset register to the application's vectors before jumping.

sides.text: What register sets Cortex-M's vector table location?

more.text: VTOR.
Avoid printf with floats, use link-time optimization, and strip unused code to fit small flash.

sides.text: Which compiler option favors small code?

more.text: -Os.
Power levels are microwatts to milliwatts, so devices store energy in capacitors and wake rarely. Needs ultra-low-power design.

sides.text: Where does an energy-harvesting node often store energy?

more.text: In a capacitor or supercapacitor.
Longer advertising and connection intervals save energy but slow discovery and response.

sides.text: What trade-off does a longer BLE connection interval bring?

more.text: Lower energy use but higher latency.
0: at most once. 1: at least once (duplicates possible). 2: exactly once (more overhead).

sides.text: Which MQTT QoS delivers exactly once?

more.text: QoS 2.
CoAP uses UDP with small headers. LwM2M builds device management on it.
UDP.
Matter defines device behavior over Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and Thread. Thread is a low-power IPv6 mesh.
A low-power IPv6 mesh network.
Each device gets its own certificate or key at manufacture, enabling mutual TLS and revocation.

sides.text: Why give each device a unique credential?

more.text: So one compromised device can be revoked without affecting the rest.
Allows up to 64 data bytes and a faster data phase than classic CAN's 8 bytes.

sides.text: How many data bytes can a CAN FD frame carry?

more.text: Up to 64.

sides.text: Standard software architecture and faster buses

more.text: AUTOSAR standardizes layers of automotive software. Automotive Ethernet gives 100 Mbit/s to multi-gigabit links over a single pair.

sides.text: Which standard defines a layered automotive software architecture?

more.text: AUTOSAR.

sides.text: Analyze failures and split safety goals

more.text: FMEA lists failure modes, effects, and detection. ASIL decomposition splits a high-level requirement across independent elements.
How components can fail and the effects.
Two cores run the same code and a comparator flags differences. ECC memory corrects single-bit errors.
Faults, by comparing two cores' outputs.

sides.text: Refresh too early or too late resets

more.text: The refresh must come within a time window, catching runaway code that refreshes constantly.
To catch code that refreshes the watchdog too early.

sides.text: Skip periodic ticks to save power

more.text: The RTOS stops the periodic timer interrupt when idle and wakes for the next scheduled event.
Wake-ups, and therefore power.
Motion changes the channel over time. Coherence time is roughly 0.423 / f_D.

sides.text: 2 GHz carrier and 30 m/s. What is the maximum Doppler shift?

more.text: Multipath delay spread makes the channel frequency-selective once the signal bandwidth exceeds the coherence bandwidth.

sides.text: σ = 1 µs. What is the coherence bandwidth?

more.text: About 200 kHz.
The prefix must exceed the maximum channel delay to avoid intersymbol interference, but it costs overhead.

sides.text: What must the cyclic prefix exceed?

more.text: The channel's maximum delay spread.
OFDM has high peaks that stress amplifiers. Clipping and tone reservation reduce them. LTE's uplink uses SC-FDMA, which has lower PAPR.

sides.text: Why does LTE use SC-FDMA in the uplink?

more.text: Lower PAPR, which suits battery-powered phones.

sides.text: Match the rate to the channel

more.text: Better channels use higher-order modulation and less coding. Poor channels fall back to robust settings.

sides.text: What does AMC change as SNR rises?

more.text: Uses higher-order modulation and higher code rates.
Hybrid ARQ stores failed packets and combines them with retransmissions, improving the chance of decoding.

sides.text: What does HARQ do with failed packets?

more.text: Combines them with retransmissions.
Prioritizes users whose current rate is high relative to their average, serving good channels without starving others.
Total throughput and fairness among users.
5G allows separate logical networks with different guarantees, such as low latency or high bandwidth.

sides.text: What does a 5G network slice provide?

more.text: A virtual network with tailored performance guarantees.
Millimeter waves lose more over distance and are blocked by bodies and walls. Oxygen absorption peaks near 60 GHz.

sides.text: Which obstacle strongly affects mmWave links?

more.text: Blockage by walls and bodies.
The base station sweeps synchronization signal blocks, and the device reports the best beam for tracking.
Alignment between narrow beams and the device.
Neighboring cells that reuse the same pilot sequences interfere in channel estimation, limiting gains.
Reuse of the same pilots across cells.
Gain and phase mismatch between I and Q create image components. DC offset appears at the carrier. Digital compensation corrects them.

sides.text: Which receiver type commonly suffers I/Q imbalance?

more.text: Direct-conversion (zero-IF).
Offsets cause loss of subcarrier orthogonality. Receivers estimate it from preambles and correct it.

sides.text: What does CFO destroy in OFDM?

more.text: Subcarrier orthogonality.
A numerically controlled oscillator mixes the band to baseband, then CIC and FIR filters decimate the sample rate.

sides.text: Which filters commonly decimate cheaply in a DDC?

more.text: CIC filters.
An RF front end, ADC, and FPGA or CPU implement modulation and filtering in software. RTL-SDR and USRP are examples.
Most signal processing is done in software or programmable logic.
Split a wideband signal into many channels with one prototype filter and an FFT.

sides.text: What do polyphase filter banks do?

more.text: Split a wide band into many channels efficiently.

sides.text: Chirps turn range into a beat frequency

more.text: The beat between transmitted and received chirps is proportional to range. Resolution = c / (2B).

sides.text: B = 4 GHz. What is the range resolution?

more.text: About 3.75 cm.

sides.text: A 2D FFT over fast and slow time

more.text: FFT across samples gives range. FFT across chirps gives Doppler (speed).

sides.text: Which two quantities does range–Doppler processing give?

more.text: Range and radial velocity.
sin θ = λΔφ / (2π d) for two antennas spaced d apart.

sides.text: What measurement gives a signal's arrival angle with two antennas?

more.text: The phase difference between them.
Time-of-flight on very wide bandwidth resolves position to centimeters. Used in digital car keys and tracking tags.

sides.text: Why can UWB measure distance so precisely?

more.text: Its very wide bandwidth gives fine timing resolution.
Successive-cancellation decoding approaches capacity. 5G uses them for control channels.
Control channels.

sides.text: Fit the code to the channel

more.text: Rate matching adjusts bits to the allocated resources. Interleaving spreads burst errors so decoders can fix them.
Burst errors.
Compare the likelihood of the data under each hypothesis. Neyman–Pearson maximizes detection for a fixed false-alarm rate.

sides.text: What does Neyman–Pearson fix while maximizing detection?

more.text: The false-alarm probability.
No unbiased estimator can have lower variance than the bound, setting limits on accuracy, such as in timing or frequency estimation.

sides.text: What does the Cramér–Rao bound limit?

more.text: The variance of unbiased estimators.

sides.text: Detect if a band is in use

more.text: Energy detection is simple but weak at low SNR. Cognitive radios use sensing to reuse idle spectrum.

sides.text: Which technique detects a band's use by measuring power?

more.text: Energy detection.
IEEE 802.1 TSN adds time synchronization, scheduling, and reservation for bounded latency in industry and vehicles.

sides.text: What does TSN guarantee on Ethernet?

more.text: Bounded, predictable latency.
A 5G service class aiming for about 1 ms latency and very high reliability, for industrial and safety uses.
About 1 ms.
3GPP adds satellite and high-altitude platforms to extend coverage. Long delays and Doppler need adaptations.
Coverage via satellites and high-altitude platforms.
